newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso closes lower at 1,015.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso closes lower at 1,015.

text.p: Colombia's peso closed lower Wednesday for the second consecutive day, after hitting its highest level since January 11 in trading early Tuesday.
The peso, which hit an intraday high of 1,009.10 to the dollar, closed at 1,015, well off Tuesday's high of 1,005.
It was knocked off the previous day's high by a central bank announcement that it would intervene in the interbank market if the peso strengthened beyond 1,005.

The market was jittery Wednesday following comments by Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo, who said the government still hopes to meet its target of a 13.5 percent devaluation of the peso this year to help make Colombian exports more attractive abroad.

But A member of the central bank's board of directors played down the significance of Ocampo's remarks in a Reuter interview, saying the bank had no intention of altering the peso's daily floating rate exchange band anytime soon.
The peso has lost 3.0 percent of its value against the dollar so far this year and has strengthened considerably since early June, when it reached a low of 1,074 to the dollar.
Dealers reported 253 trades in Wednesday's session for a total of $90 million and said demand for dollars had come mostly from banks that were short of foreign currency.
